"""Bracket-balance checking that ignores double-quoted strings."""

_PAIRS = {')': '(', ']': '[', '}': '{'}


def balanced(s):
    """Return True if every (, [ and { in s is closed by the matching
    bracket in the right order.

    Text inside double-quoted strings is ignored.  Inside such a string a
    backslash escapes the next character, so \" does not end the string.
    An unterminated string makes the whole input unbalanced.
    """
    stack = []
    i = 0
    n = len(s)
    while i < n:
        c = s[i]
        if c == '"':
            # Skip the string literal.
            i += 1
            closed = False
            while i < n:
                if s[i] == '\\':
                    i += 2
                    continue
                if s[i] == '"':
                    i += 1
                    closed = True
                    break
                i += 1
            if not closed:
                return False
            continue
        if c in '([{':
            stack.append(c)
        elif c in ')]}':
            if not stack or stack.pop() != _PAIRS[c]:
                return False
        i += 1
    return not stack
